symbols.name: selected chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of selected address chunks.
symbols.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ selected address chunks of $K$ bits, at a common offset, in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes; here $D$ is the number of selected address chunks, not the second chunk value of [Fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md), and $D$ is not the source group of [Matrix shear by triangular factorization](matrix-shear.md).

symbols.name: selected axis count
symbols.meaning: The number of selected axes in a group.
symbols.quote: A group of $e=mf$ selected axes ($e$ is the number of selected axes, not the number of digits in a chunk as on [Fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md)) has $m$ slots of $f$ axes; a column holds one bit per slot, in $\mathbb F_2^m.$

symbols.name: array
symbols.meaning: An array acted on by the diagonal operator.
symbols.quote: where the diagonal operator $\mathcal S_D$ acts on an array $z$ by $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x).$

symbols.name: diagonal phase operator
symbols.meaning: The diagonal operator multiplying the value at address x by i to the sum of the selected bits.
symbols.quote: where the diagonal operator $\mathcal S_D$ acts on an array $z$ by $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x).$

symbols.name: basis-change matrix
symbols.meaning: An invertible F_2 matrix whose first columns are the residual basis vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $\Gamma$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with first columns $v_\xi$ and $\mathcal P_\Gamma:x\mapsto\Gamma x$ an address permutation.

symbols.name: address permutation
symbols.meaning: The address permutation moving the value at x to Gamma x.
symbols.quote: Let $\Gamma$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with first columns $v_\xi$ and $\mathcal P_\Gamma:x\mapsto\Gamma x$ an address permutation.

symbols.name: residual basis index
symbols.meaning: The index of the residual basis vectors.
symbols.quote: with residual basis vectors $v_\xi$ indexed by $\xi,$ $\eta_\xi=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

symbols.name: edge sign
symbols.meaning: The sign plus or minus one of the xi-th residual basis vector's exponent.
symbols.quote: with residual basis vectors $v_\xi$ indexed by $\xi,$ $\eta_\xi=\pm1,$ $C_v=aI+bX_v$ and $X_v$ shifting a column by $v.$

symbols.name: individual chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of leading chunks given individual C kernels.
symbols.quote: So the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks get individual $C$ kernels, in $O(V\log d),$ and their bits form a row index of range at least $W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil}.$

symbols.name: operation-chain bound
symbols.meaning: A bound on the arithmetic operations on a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient.
symbols.quote: Let $\chi(e)$ bound the operations on a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient

symbols.name: invocation operation bound
symbols.meaning: The bound on arithmetic operations in one invocation of the network.
symbols.quote: ($E$ below is an operation bound, not the first tensor factor of [Tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md); $E$ is likewise not the edge residual of the phase frames page)

symbols.name: level growth factor
symbols.meaning: The sum s plus E, the factor by which each internal level multiplies the chain bound.

symbols.name: chain bound
symbols.meaning: Any bound on a chain's operation count that is at least one.

symbols.name: exponent
symbols.meaning: The least positive exponent j with m to the j at least Psi.
symbols.quote: With $\vartheta=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge\Psi\}$ (an exponent of $m,$ not a digit count)

symbols.name: guard constant
symbols.meaning: The constant 128 m Psi squared in the reserved extra bits Delta.

relations.quote: $C^{\otimes e}$ is computed by the network of [Binary phase frames](phase-frames.md), with $W$ wires and $s$ smaller calls.
The layer obeys the recursion of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md).
[Packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md) XORs selected bits by cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges plus a repair of exceptional addresses.
The layer is evaluated in [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md).

derivations.quote: With $\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i),$ the [Two-point kernel C](phase-kernel.md) $C=aI+bX$ satisfies $H_0=b\,\mathsf SC\mathsf S,$ $C^2=X$ and $C^4=I$

Apply $\mathcal P_\Gamma^{-1},$ then $(C^{\eta_\xi})^{\otimes f}$ to the $f$ bits of slot $\xi,$ then $\mathcal P_\Gamma:$ one child on $f=e/m$ axes per residual vector, exactly $s$ in all. Negative powers add no child: $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$ with $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1).$

With $x_1,\dots,x_D$ the selected bits of an address $x,$ this gives $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D,$ where the diagonal operator $\mathcal S_D$ acts on an array $z$ by $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x).$ Here $z$ is an array, not an address suffix as on [Fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md), and $z$ is not a binary vector as on [Binary phase frames](phase-frames.md). Phases and $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ are exact Gaussian dyadic, leaving $C^{\otimes D}.$

Elimination writes $\Gamma$ as at most $m(m-1)+3m$ row additions (a swap is three). Each XORs selected bits of one slot into another; [Packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md) XORs selected bits by cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges plus a repair of exceptional addresses. Their number is fixed, so the basis change and its inverse on $e$ axis chunks cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$

Rows go to the $W$ wire roles by index mod $W,$ so children have volume $V/W$ if the row count stays divisible by $W$ through $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels. So the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks get individual $C$ kernels, in $O(V\log d),$ and their bits form a row index of range at least $W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil}.$ Zero rows pad each block to a multiple of that, making the row count at depth $j$ divisible by $W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil-j};$ fewer rows are added than the block holds, so the volume at most doubles. With $\beta=\tfrac12$ and $F(e)$ the time divided by volume,
$$F(e)\le \tfrac sW F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)\ (e\ge d^\beta),\qquad F(e)=O(e)\ (e<d^\beta),$$
The layer obeys the recursion of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md). As $s/W\le m^\sigma,$ $\sigma<1,$ internal levels sum geometrically, leaves add $O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)}),$ and $\log d$ pieces give $O(d^{\lambda'}).$

Let $\chi(e)$ bound the operations on a chain from an input to an intermediate coefficient ($E$ below is an operation bound, not the first tensor factor of [Tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md); $E$ is likewise not the edge residual of the phase frames page). An invocation has at most $12W$ gates, each taking at most $2W^2$ operations (each output sums at most $W$ terms); inverse-child corrections take at most $4s,$ other corrections $4W+4.$ As $s<Wm,$ the total $24W^3+4s+4W+4$ is below $E=64(W+m+1)^3.$ Chains concatenate the $s$ children; a leaf pair takes eight operations:
$$\chi(e)\le s\chi(e/m)+E,\qquad \chi(e)\le8e\ (\text{leaf}).$$
With $\Psi=s+E,$ $s\varphi+E\le\Psi\varphi$ for any bound $\varphi\ge1,$ so $\chi(e)\le8d\Psi^{\lceil\log_md\rceil+1}.$ With $\vartheta=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge\Psi\}$ (an exponent of $m,$ not a digit count), $\Psi^{\lceil\log_md\rceil+1}\le\Psi^{\log_md+2}=\Psi^2d^{\log_m\Psi}\le\Psi^2d^\vartheta,$ so $\chi(e)\le8\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+1}.$ The at most $md$ pieces add $8m\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+2},$ individual kernels $8d,$ diagonals and $b^D$ at most $\lfloor D/2\rfloor+9.$ The total is at most $8m\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+2}+18d<128m\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+3}\le\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil,$ with $C_0=128m\Psi^2,$ $C_1=\max\{20,\vartheta+3\}.$

A depth-$\ell$ value lies in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell,$ since addition at most doubles modulus and halving adds a denominator bit. So $p+\Delta$ fractional and $\Delta+3$ integer and sign bits per real component represent every intermediate coefficient exactly
Absolute row sums multiply under tensor products, so each row of $\mathcal H=H_0^{\otimes D}$ has absolute row sum one. Hence $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays
Truncation toward zero cannot increase a component's absolute value and changes it by less than $2^{-p},$ so $Q_p$ keeps the disk, with $\|Q_p(\mathcal Hz)-\mathcal Hz\|_\infty<\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$
